leading_positions.synthesis: Five of eight members prefer B014 as a sole prize part. All five name the same three laureates (MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer) and word the citation around the prediction of flat bands at the magic angle plus the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states, not around the pairing mechanism. Shared: a prediction-then-experiment structure, reproduction by many groups, no overlap with a recent prize. Not shared: how much weight to give the unsettled superconducting mechanism and twist-angle disorder, and whether Eva Andrei's STM flat-band work or Yuan Cao's first authorship should alter the credited set. Several supporters (Danielsson, Johansson, Olsson, Eriksson) say they moved toward B014 after reading the openings, and at least Danielsson, Olsson and Mehlig make support conditional on an expert check of the Andrei question.

Three members include optical lattice clocks (Katori and Ye) in their preferred configuration; Kroll and Lindroth as a sole prize, Pearce as one of two parts. All three name the same two laureates and word the citation around the lattice clock or magic-wavelength principle at the 10^-18 level, and all cite cross-laboratory validation of the uncertainty budgets. All three also raise the same reservations: overlap with the 2005 (Hall, Hansch) and 2012 (Wineland) prizes, the pending SI redefinition of the second, and credit for the Paris, PTB, JILA and RIKEN groups. They differ on whether the clock is a new-regime discovery or a measurement capability, a doubt raised by Danielsson and Mehlig (no one else ranks it first) and by Eriksson, who calls it precision engineering built on the 2005 recognition.

Only the chair prefers a two-part prize pairing IceCube (Halzen alone) with the lattice clock (Katori, Ye). The chair's own file concedes that B016 has the thinnest support, that a single credited name for a collaboration-scale discovery is hard to defend on the packet alone, and that the part should not carry the prize unless outside experts supply a defensible set of names. Danielsson, who opened with B016 first, has moved his preferred configuration to B014 but lists B016 as his first alternative; Eriksson, Johansson and Lindroth regard the one-name allocation as the weakest attribution on the shortlist. The two parts are not shared with any other member's configuration.

areas_of_agreement: No member's preferred configuration contains a part other than B014, B013 or B016; B041 appears only as an alternative (Danielsson, Eriksson, Mehlig, Olsson), as do B046 (Johansson, Kroll), B031 (Lindroth), B021 (Olsson) and B014 (Kroll, Lindroth, Pearce).

Within each configuration the laureate sets are identical across members: MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Bistritzer for B014; Katori and Ye for B013. The disagreement is about whether to build on them, not about who is named.

Members on all sides agree that a citation should name phenomena or capabilities actually observed and independently reproduced, not an explanation of the superconducting pairing mechanism in twisted bilayer graphene.

Members agree that the Andrei and Cao question for B014, the Halzen-only credit for B016, and the Girvin and Devoret credit for B046 cannot be settled from the supplied packet and need outside expert reports.

Several members (Mehlig, Eriksson, Danielsson, Johansson, Olsson) tie their view of B046 to the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits; no member includes B046 in a preferred configuration.
scientific_disputes: Whether the unresolved pairing mechanism and twist-angle disorder in magic-angle graphene make B014 premature (Lindroth, Kroll, Danielsson's caveat) or whether a reproduced phenomenon with an open mechanism is sufficient, as earlier prizes show (Eriksson, Johansson, Mehlig, Olsson).

Whether the optical lattice clock is a distinct physical idea, a state-insensitive trap that averages over many atoms (Pearce, Kroll, Lindroth), or an incremental refinement of precision frequency metrology (Eriksson, Mehlig, Danielsson).

Whether the clock is a discovery of new physics or a measurement capability whose payoff, such as redshift tests, varying-constant limits and dark-matter searches, still has to materialise (Danielsson, Lindroth's own caveat).

Whether the 2018 experiments confirmed the prediction. Johansson, Olsson and Eriksson note that the flat-band prediction does not by itself predict the insulating or superconducting states, so the discovery of those phases is the more original step.
Whether the diffuse IceCube flux, as opposed to identification of its sources, is a sufficient basis for a prize (Pearce, Danielsson); Lindroth notes the source of most of the flux is unexplained.
attribution_disputes: B014: Eva Andrei's early STM evidence of flat-band localisation is called independent support by Mehlig and Olsson, and a lesser claim by Eriksson. All five supporters flag the issue and none resolves it. Yuan Cao, first author of the 2018 papers, falls outside any three-person cut.

B014: Mehlig and Olsson would keep Bistritzer, and so would not make room for Andrei by dropping a theorist. Mehlig notes Jarillo-Herrero alone is an alternative cut. Earlier twisted-bilayer theory (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto; Suarez Morell; Shallcross) is also not covered.

B013: the priority of the first Sr lattice clock demonstrations (Katori in Tokyo, Ye at JILA, the Paris group) and the contributions of Lemonde, Lisdat, Sterr and Ludlow are unresolved. Kroll and Lindroth both say they rely on memory for dates.
B013: whether Ye's contribution is the lattice clock itself or is still shaded by his association with the Hall frequency-comb lineage.

B016: one credited name (Halzen) for a km3 collaboration with AMANDA predecessors. Pearce, Danielsson, Eriksson and Johansson all call this the thinnest attribution on the shortlist and request expert input.
B046 (not in any configuration): the Girvin and Devoret credit and the position of Blais, Wallraff and Schoelkopf relative to the 2025 prize.
B041 (alternative only): omission of Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Mele and Fu, the 2D versus 3D split between Molenkamp and Hasan, and overlap with the 2016 topological prize.
maturity_disputes: B014 is less than a decade old and the pairing mechanism is open. Lindroth, Kroll and Danielsson treat this as a real risk; Eriksson, Johansson, Mehlig and Olsson treat it as separate from the maturity of the discovered phases.

B013 has high experimental maturity, with cross-checked uncertainty budgets at 10^-18, but Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce disagree on whether the SI redefinition of the second must precede recognition. Lindroth says it should not be a requirement.

Whether overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes counts against the clock (Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce raise it against their own candidate) or is irrelevant if the citation is written narrowly around the lattice.
B021 (alternative to Olsson only): Olsson sees nearly four decades of confirmation as overdue recognition; Mehlig sees a foundational tool, with Landauer and Buttiker uncredited.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson (Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology, Chalmers) declares a specific connection to B046 and says he should recuse from any final vote on it, treating his opening first-place ranking as informed by that proximity.

Pearce (chair) flags a possible recusal question on B016: his collaborations are PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and XL-Calibur, not IceCube, but IceCube is a neighbouring astroparticle community. He asks the committee to rule.

Kroll spent a year in John Hall's laboratory during his PhD and has a WACQT role that overlaps institutionally with Chalmers, so he asks to weigh the comb overlap neutrally and notes the Chalmers link matters only if B046 becomes a preferred candidate.
Lindroth notes atomic physics is her home field (close to B013, B031, B017) and that she is a long-time collaborator of Anne L'Huillier; she treats this as a possible bias, not a recusal.
Eriksson chaired the 2025 committee for the superconducting-circuit prize, relevant to how he weighs B046 but not a personal connection to any candidate.
Danielsson, Mehlig and Olsson report no specific conflict with the shortlist. Olsson notes only a shared first name with Eva Y. Andrei and no known relationship.
questions_for_round2: For B014: can members say, from the primary literature and expert reports, whether Andrei's STM flat-band results (2010-2017) established the flat-band physics independently of the 2018 transport results, and does that change the credited set or only corroborate the prediction? Is Cao's role decisive enough to alter the cut?

For B014: if the citation names only the prediction of flat bands and the observation of correlated and superconducting phases, do Lindroth and Kroll still regard the open pairing mechanism and twist-angle disorder as a maturity bar, and what specific evidence would move them?

For B013: can Lindroth and Kroll state whether Ye's credited contribution is the lattice clock itself or still shaded by the frequency-comb lineage, and do the first Sr lattice-clock demonstrations (Tokyo, JILA, Paris) support a Katori and Ye pair or a wider set?

For B013: is the clock a discovery or a measurement capability, and does the committee want the pending SI redefinition of the second, or a demonstrated new-physics result, as a condition of recognition?

For B016: what second or third name, if any, can the experts defend alongside Halzen, and failing that, does the chair's two-part configuration have any standing if B016 cannot be credited? Should the chair step back from any B016 vote?

Between a sole B014 prize and a B013 prize, which supporters would accept the other as their lead part, and would anyone support a two-part B014 with B013 given Mehlig's concern that it dilutes the strongest case?

Does Johansson's declared closeness to B046, together with the 2025 overlap, mean B046 is out of consideration for 2026, or does any member want to argue it is separable from the 2025 recognition in scientific content?
Should B041 remain on the table at all, given four members list it only as an alternative and cite the 2016 overlap and the credit problem (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Mele, Fu)?
summary.chair_observation: On the explicit round-1 configurations, B014 has five supporters, B013 has three (one of them as half of a two-part prize), and B016 has one, the chair's own. Within each configuration the laureate sets agree, so the open questions are about three cases: Andrei and Cao for B014, whether the lattice clock is a new discovery for B013, and the Halzen-only credit for B016. Several members changed their preferred configuration after the openings, so these counts reflect round 1 only. The chair's own configuration is the minority one and should be weighed as such. Everything here depends on the members' own statements and on dates recalled from memory, which expert reports should check.
